findings.title: Narrow F5-only seven-slot GDT
findings.assessment: Read actual F3Context: five entries followed by original normal/emergency TSS objects. Authorization permits a separate extension rather than resizing that structure. Proposal03 follows precisely this narrow route and does not imply current USER descriptors or current CPL3 support.

findings.title: Exact preservation of original slots0-4
findings.assessment: Original slots are null, kernel code08, data10, normal TSS18 and emergency20. Actual cpu_readback requires busy normal descriptor8b and available emergency89. Copying actual40 bytes after original successful installation preserves these live states; reconstructing the original available normal descriptor would be incorrect. Pre/post raw comparison is mandatory.

findings.title: Decode appended descriptors
findings.assessment: Independently bit-decoded fb/f3 access bytes: P1,DPL3,S1,accessed1; code executable/readable/nonconforming and data writable. Both base0,effective limitffffffff,G1,DB1,L0. Accessed pre-set avoids CPU mutation of expected bytes. This changes only F5 table, not inherited kernel99/93 descriptors.

findings.title: Selectors derive from slots and RPL
findings.assessment: Computed (5<<3)|3=2b and (6<<3)|3=33, TI0, RPL3. Existing kernel08/10 and TSS18/20 meanings remain. Correct descriptor DPL plus USER paging, not selector RPL by itself, enables entry.

findings.title: GDTR backing, length and verification boundary
findings.assessment: Seven u64 slots occupy56 bytes, limit55; original actual verifier insists limit39 and original static address. Proposal uses original verify only before switch and separate F5 readback afterward. New aligned static table must be entirely present supervisor kernel-image backing and retained for hardware lifetime.

findings.title: TSS base, byte limit and busy state
findings.assessment: Actual Tss has104 bytes and descriptor() produces limit103 and full32-bit base. Proposal copies busy normal8b and available emergency89 with original bases, no moves or reset. Current cached TR state remains loaded; actual TR and hidden-cache/descriptor evidence remains a future guest obligation.

findings.title: LGDT/LTR and segment reload sequencing
findings.assessment: Original installation reloads CS08 by far jump, data/SS10 and then LTR18 exactly once. F5 switches GDTR only after this succeeds and never retries LTR on a busy descriptor. Identical original segment descriptors preserve cached semantics. New user data loads occur only after final kernel-DS-dependent access and before IRETD.

findings.title: Normal/emergency TSS compatibility
findings.assessment: normal_state supplies transition ESP0/SS0; emergency_state retains independent CR3, stack, selectors and assembly entry. Actual emergency assembly snapshots task-entry ESP/TR/CR3/error without interpreting an F2 frame. Proposal preserves both objects/stack layouts and treats every #DF as non-F5-PASS.

findings.title: Double-fault task gate and IF discipline
findings.assessment: Read actual IDT8 constant0000850000200000: present DPL0 task gate to20. F5 excludes8 when replacing gates and keeps slot4 target unchanged. It must not invoke InterruptTable::load because that routine executes STI. IF0 gate installation and task-gate raw verification are required by proposal, not proven by this review.

findings.title: Inherited F2/F3/F4 compatibility and shared macro decision
findings.assessment: Independently accept source-shared parameterized stub/common macros as preserving the fixed F2 entry contract; exact same common address is not an intrinsic ABI requirement. Default F2 symbol identities, instructions, bridge target and68-byte layout must survive modulo relocations, with actual emitted comparison. F5-only gates select the alternate bridge, while default F3/F4 paths and serial remain untouched. This approves a design direction, not a new independent frame decoder or an inherited Ring0 result relabelled CPL3.

findings.title: IRETD outer-privilege frame and flags
findings.assessment: Proposed32-bit pushes SS33,ESP40400000,EFLAGS2,CS2b,EIP yield the required pop order EIP/CS/flags/ESP/SS. Scenario validation precedes selector changes; no return continuation or arbitrary USER input. Entry flags clear IF,DF,IOPL,NT,VM,RF and other nonfixed bits; later fault-saved RF/DF intentionally differ. Page-end ESP is valid because first PUSH touches403ffffc and POP restores it. Require emitted operand-size and finite target audit.

findings.title: Conditional tail origin and pointer gate
findings.assessment: Existing synthetic_transition_tail is explicitly nonproduction and accepts broader nonzero origins. It is not the F5 unsafe decoder. Same-ring/unsupported/nested/#DF paths never read an assumed tail; nested latch refusal precedes decoding. Emitted control-flow proof and host refusal tests remain mandatory.

findings.title: All six payload encodings and image boundaries
findings.assessment: Parsed each actual proposal hex string and computed offsets independently. Shared12-byte prologue clears EAX, copies CS into AX, pushes/pops5a17c0de, sets DF; PUSH/POP are real USER stack operations. B c605 stores byte7e to40000800; C8b0d reads07c01000; Df4 HLT; Ee680 OUT80,AL; F8b0d reads403fe000. Each intended opcode is at entry+12 with UD2 fallback. Six64-byte slots occupy100..27f without touching PREFIX0/DATA800. Constructed page digests are design derivations only, not actual guest bytes or new artifacts.

findings.title: Both-level USER/PRESENT/RW and ordering
findings.assessment: Read actual supervisor inventory and install: code P/U/runtime RO at0, stack P/RW/U/runtime at1023, intervening leaves absent; final PDE256 P/RW/U after leases/pins and leaves. Validator permits only hardware A/D changes on mapped entries, absent leaves stay0. C needs actual present supervisor translation, not address-based assumption; refuse launch otherwise. F5 preserves CR3, supervisor aliases, guards and non-PAE profile without granting USER elsewhere.

findings.title: Exact fault/error/CR2 predicates
findings.assessment: Derived A6/0, B14/7 (present write user), C14/5 (present read user denied supervisor), D13/0 HLT, E13/0 I/O privilege denial, F14/4 (absent user read). PF CR2 exact40000800/07c01000/403fe000; GP error exactly0; full32-bit equality rejects every unsupported error flag. Fallback UD2, earlier IRET fault or wrong PC cannot pass. OUT denial is architectural no-permitted-transfer evidence, not external-device trace.

findings.title: Fault-saved RF exactness and negative control
findings.assessment: Independently calculated RF10000+DF400+ZF40+PF4+bit1=10446; undefined AF permits10456 only. All tested #UD/#PF/#GP are fault-class and retrieved architecture explicitly requires pushed RF1 except instruction-breakpoint #DB. Actual F2/F4 source also ORs preflags with RF. Proposal03 retains entry flags2 but demands saved10446/10456 and RF0 rejection. AF is the only masked bit, not IF/DF or arbitrary discrepancies.

findings.title: CPU selector padding versus software saves
findings.assessment: CPU CS/oldSS are32-bit slots but low16 defines selector; retrieved architecture describes padded far-pointer pushes. Proposal checks CS low16 before optional reads and oldSS low16, records raw high halves unconstrained. Software saves compare full33 because XOR EAX precedes16-bit MOV. Nonzero-high acceptance/wrong-low rejection controls are frozen.
